subject.title: [Feature]: Control UI should show compact run progress for long or multi-agent tasks

question: What canonical Gateway activity contract and Control UI phase taxonomy should OpenClaw expose for active chat runs before implementing the compact progress strip?
rationale: This affects public Gateway/session semantics and user-facing Control UI behavior; current main lacks the contract, and the open PR candidates do not yet settle scope, proof, or compatibility.

options.title: Approve Gateway-Backed Activity Model
options.body: Define the session activity fields, event/resync behavior, attention states, and safe UI phases first, then land a focused Control UI presentation.

options.title: Narrow To UI-Only Coarse Status
options.body: Allow a smaller UI-only extension, accepting that subagent, reconnect, and delayed-delivery truth may remain incomplete until the gateway contract lands.

options.title: Defer Behind Broader Activity Issue
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until the broader session activity issue and candidate PR direction are resolved.

recommendation.title: Approve Gateway-Backed Activity Model
recommendation.body: Define the session activity fields, event/resync behavior, attention states, and safe UI phases first, then land a focused Control UI presentation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent Gateway/protocol history route the active code path through Vincent Koc, and the decision is primarily about Gateway/session semantics plus Control UI presentation.
